Problem Statement

This is the old quantity modal. Its job was to sell bulk deals.

  1. 🛍️Product with slab pricing
  2. 👆Retailer taps Add
  3. 📱This modal opens

Tap the pins to see why it didn't work

  1. The whole point of the screen, shrunk to one thin row of small text.

  2. Payment, delivery and return terms filled the prime spot.

  3. Leaving no room to compare slabs or show savings.

So retailers couldn't answer

How does price change with quantity?Which slab is the better deal?What do I do next?

What the data said

#1
Drop-off point

Highest exit rate in the whole buying flow.

1–9
Pieces per order

Qty defaulted to the lowest slab, so sellers rejected many orders.

Iterations I have tried

Each version kept what worked.

✕Too much info, cramped buttons, no reason to buy more
✓All slabs visible, info grouped well
✕Quantity and total too far apart
✓Progress cue added, lighter than V1
✕Policies moved to other entry points
✓Slabs first, margin bar moves as you type

Why V3 won

Bulk value up front

Big slab cards. The right one selects itself as you type.

Margin as progress

See how close the next discount is.

Policies moved out

Still in cart and seller catalogue.

Looking back

🤖Used AI as a thinking partner

To explore ideas, validate directions and iterate faster. It led to solutions like the progress indicator.

🤝Stakeholder management is key

Aligning stakeholders on what truly mattered sharpened visual priority and put focus on the key decision-making elements.

👥Collaborated closely with cross-functional teams

Continuous feedback helped refine and successfully deliver the final design.

🎁Future scope for free gifts and other incentives

Today it focuses on quantity-based discounts. Next, the modal should clearly show every bulk benefit, like free items.

🔎Conduct deeper user research

To better understand how retailers decide on bulk purchases, and optimize how incentives are presented.

📊Continue iterating on metrics and feedback

Keep improving clarity and usability based on product metrics and real user behaviour.
